title: Watchdog probes death of man jailed for intoxication
article: The Special Investigations Unit is looking into the death of a 46- year-old man who died after being arrested and put in police cells.
The civilian agency probes deaths, serious injuries or sexual assaults involving police. It lays criminal charges in about 3 per cent of the cases it investigates.
SIU spokesperson Rose Hong said two Niagara police officers arrested Grant Spielmacher for public intoxication near James and Church streets in downtown St. Catharines at about 5:30 p.m. Monday.

He was found in medical distress in a cell at central police station about a block away at about 8:40 p.m. Police said he was given medical help and taken to Hotel Dieu Hospital where efforts to revive him were unsuccessful. Hong would not reveal the nature of the "medical distress" or say where he died in relation to the trip to the hospital.
Investigators are still waiting for the results of an autopsy that was to be performed yesterday and want to talk to the doctor before pinpointing the time and cause of death.
She said the SIU has assigned five investigators to the case, including two forensic experts, and have designated the two officers who arrested Spielmacher as "witness officers" in the investigation.
This means the SIU believes they have relevant information about the case. They must provide statements about the incident and could be compelled to hand over their notes if the SIU wants them.

Hong said the agency hasn't designated anyone as a "subject officer," who would be an officer whose conduct could have contributed to Spielmacher's death. This suggests the agency doesn't suspect any officer of misconduct at this stage. Hong said the SIU could designate a subject officer later based on the evidence. She said investigators planned to canvass the area near Church and James streets yesterday for people who might have seen Spielmacher being arrested.
